title: Petopia release-blocker fixes: new logo system + TypeScript-imported image strategy with consistent fallbacks

requirements.summary: Regenerate Petopia logo system and enforce a single reusable Logo component used everywhere, with brand text exactly “Petopia” and no “Premium” in any logo/alt/fallback contexts.
acceptanceCriteria: Searching the codebase for the string "Premium" returns zero instances in logo/brand contexts (including SVG text, image names, alt/fallback content).
All pages that render a logo (global header/footer, /account/login, /account/signup, /cart, /checkout, /payment, and all confirmation pages) display the exact wordmark text “Petopia”.

There is exactly one reusable frontend component/module responsible for rendering the logo (icon + wordmark) and all other logo renderings delegate to it (no duplicate inline SVGs or hardcoded logo paths).

file_operations.description: Add the generated Petopia primary logo icon asset at this exact path (wordmark must be exactly “Petopia”; no “Premium” anywhere).
Add the generated Petopia horizontal lockup (icon + wordmark) asset at this exact path (wordmark must be exactly “Petopia”; no “Premium” anywhere).
Create a single TypeScript module that imports and re-exports the brand logo assets (icon + lockup) so all in-app logo rendering uses TypeScript imports as the single source of truth.

Refactor BrandLogo to exclusively render the new imported logo assets from frontend/src/assets/brand.ts (no string paths), ensure alt/ARIA/fallback text is exactly “Petopia”, and remove any legacy logo references. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Ensure navbar delegates all logo rendering to BrandLogo with no inline logo markup or hardcoded asset paths, and verify any brand/alt/fallback text remains exactly “Petopia”. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Ensure footer delegates all logo rendering to BrandLogo and remove/adjust any brand-adjacent copy that could reintroduce “Premium” in brand contexts. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Ensure the login page’s logo renders via BrandLogo only (no hardcoded logo assets) and the displayed/accessible brand text remains “Petopia”. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Ensure the signup page’s logo renders via BrandLogo only (no hardcoded logo assets) and the displayed/accessible brand text remains “Petopia”. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.
Ensure cart page header uses BrandLogo only (no hardcoded assets) and remove any legacy brand text variants. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

requirements.summary: Update favicon to a simplified icon derived from the new logo icon and ensure index.html references it as a static asset.
acceptanceCriteria: The favicon is visually recognizable at small sizes and matches the logo icon style.
frontend/index.html references the new favicon file and the favicon loads correctly in the browser tab on first load.

file_operations.description: Add/replace the generated Petopia favicon derived from the new logo icon at this exact path.
Ensure the HTML entry references the favicon via the static path /assets/generated/petopia-favicon.dim_64x64.png (favicon is the exception to the TypeScript-imported in-app image strategy).

requirements.summary: Standardize in-app images to TypeScript-imported assets by refactoring content modules and consuming pages/components so images resolve reliably across all routes (including dynamic routes).
acceptanceCriteria: In-app images (cards, heroes, galleries, thumbnails, order/cart summary images) are rendered from TypeScript imports rather than string paths like "/assets/...".
Navigation across dynamic routes (e.g., product detail, adoption species/breed/pet profile, blog topic/article) shows correct images on first load and on refresh (no broken images).
No components/pages reference broken absolute paths for in-app images (e.g., hardcoded "/assets/generated/..." in JSX for non-favicon use cases).

requirements.summary: Add consistent image loading behavior and fallbacks for lazy-loaded images so cards and detail pages never show broken-image icons or layout collapse.
acceptanceCriteria: If an image fails to load, the UI displays a consistent fallback presentation instead of a broken-image icon or layout collapse.
Key listing/detail surfaces (Products, Services, Adoption, Blog) do not show missing/broken images during normal navigation and refresh scenarios.
Lazy-loaded images use consistent settings and do not cause blank gaps during initial render (especially in grids and galleries).

Update PageHero to use AppImage for any hero images it renders (or to apply equivalent fallback behavior) so hero surfaces don’t render broken images or blank gaps.

requirements.summary: Perform a release-blocking QA sweep and fix any remaining “Premium” remnants and broken images across the sitemap, especially on Adoption/Product/Service/Blog routes and checkout flow.
acceptanceCriteria: Manual QA pass confirms the three blocker conditions (no “Premium”, no broken images, correct image loading across Adoption/Product/Service/Blog) are satisfied across routed navigation and direct URL entry (refresh).
Any discovered broken routes or broken assets are fixed as part of this task, with no regressions in cart/checkout/payment navigation.
